q: Which law is the Architecture Act of 2004?
n: RA 9266 is the Architecture Act of 2004. It repealed RA 545. It governs the registration, licensing and practice of architecture in the Philippines. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 1 and 46.

q: Which is NOT a ground for refusing registration or revoking a license?
o: Conviction of a criminal offense involving moral turpitude
n: Conviction of a political offense is expressly not a ground for refusing registration or revoking a license. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 22.

q: Under intellectual property law, who is the author of the contract drawings?
n: The architect-of-record is the author of the contract drawings. They are his intellectual property. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 33; RA 8293.

q: Section 41 of RA 9266.
o: Implementing Rules and Regulation of Code of Ethical Conduct and Standard of Professional Practice
n: Section 41 of RA 9266 provides for the Implementing Rules and Regulations, including the Code of Ethical Conduct and Standards of Professional Practice. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 41.

q: A foreign architect can practice in the Philippines provided that it must have.
n: A foreign architect allowed to practise must work with a Filipino counterpart (local architect-of-record) under a temporary/special permit. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 38.

q: The architect-of-record for a building he designed is:
n: The architect-of-record is liable (civilly) for the documents he signed and sealed. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3 and 20.

q: Drawings and specifications and other contract documents duly signed, stamped, or sealed, instruments of service, are the intellectual property and documents of the architect, whether the object for which they are made is executed or not. It shall be unlawful for any person to duplicate or make copies of said documents for use in the repetition of and for other projects or buildings, whether executed partly or in whole, without the written consent of the architect or author of said documents. What would you do if you found out that your client has reproduced your drawings and used them for another project?
n: Signed and sealed drawings, specifications and contract documents are instruments of service, the architect's intellectual property, whether or not the project is built. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 33.

q: Practicing architecture without registration or a valid permit is a misdemeanor with a fine of:
n: Practising architecture without registration or a valid permit is penalized with a fine of ₱100,000 to ₱5,000,000, or imprisonment, or both. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 29.

q: Anyone who forces an architect to work without a written contract commits a misdemeanor with a minimum fine of:
n: Forcing an architect to work without a written contract falls under the same penal clause, with a minimum fine of ₱100,000. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 29.

q: Fine (amount) for an act of malpractice in architecture by an unregistered person?
n: Malpractice in architecture by an unregistered person carries a fine starting at ₱100,000 (up to ₱5,000,000). Source: RA 9266, Sec. 29.

q: Under the SPP, contract documents (detailed designs, working drawings and specifications) are based on the approved:
n: Contract documents (detailed designs, working drawings, specifications) are based on the approved design development documents. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202.

q: Which is NOT true of a foreigner seeking to take the LEA through reciprocity?
o: Approval comes from CHED and PRC
He must be registered in his own country
n: A foreign reciprocity applicant must be registered in his own country, meet all prerequisites and show reciprocity for Filipinos. Approval is by the PRC Board, not CHED. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 27.

q: Anunlicensed graduate of BS Architecture is commissioned by his brother to design a Five-Storey Residence. He asks an RLA to sign and seal it. The RLA agrees to do it for asum of Php 500,000 and then changes his mind and files a case instead. Is there anything wrong? If yes, who will be liable for the case?
o: Nothing is wrong because it's not constructed yet
Unlicensed graduate and brother of the project
Yes, the student is liable for doing it
n: An RLA who signs and seals plans he did not prepare or supervise ("plan stamping") violates RA 9266 and the Code of Ethical Conduct, which is grounds for suspension or revocation. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 20(4) and 23.

q: Anunlicensed graduate of BS Architecture is commissioned by his brother to design a Five-Storey Residence. He asks an RLA to sign and seal it. The RLA agrees to do it for a sum of Php 500,000 and then changes his mind and files a case instead. What is the case, if ever?
n: The unlicensed graduate who designs for others and has an RLA sign the plans is practising illegally. He is liable under RA 9266's penal clause. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 29 and 31.

q: An unlicensed graduate of BS Architecture is commissioned by his brother to design a Five-Storey Residence. He asks an RLA to sign and seal it. The RLA agrees to do it for a sum of Php 500,000 and then changes his mind and files a case instead. Where should the RLA file the case?
n: Both parties are liable: the RLA for signing plans he did not prepare (administrative and penal) and the unregistered designer for illegal practice. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 20, 23 and 29.

q: In Reciprocity agreement, Filipino architects are allowed in other countries to?
n: Reciprocity agreements let Filipino architects practise the profession in the partner country on the same basis as its citizens. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 27 and 38(a).

q: What is the architect-in-charge of construction liable for?
n: The architect-in-charge of construction is liable for quality control, daily inspection reports and filing, and evaluation of construction work, so all of the above. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3; 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 204-A.

q: What is the term of a Board of Architecture member?
n: A Board of Architecture member serves a 3-year term and may be reappointed for one more full term. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 6.

q: An architect practicing alone under a DTI registration is a:
n: An architect practising alone under a DTI business name is a sole proprietor. Source: RA 9266 IRR (definitions); DTI Business Name Registration Act.

q: Which section of RA 9266 covers reciprocity?
n: Section 27 of RA 9266 covers reciprocity requirements. It allows foreigners to take the licensure exam only if their country admits Filipinos on equal terms. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 27.

q: Which section of RA 9266 is titled "Prohibition in the Practice of Architecture"?
n: Section 30 of RA 9266 is titled "Prohibition in the Practice of Architecture". Sec. 29 combines the prohibition with the penal clause. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 29–30.

q: Which section covers suspension and revocation of CORs, PICs and permits?
n: Section 23 covers suspension and revocation of Certificates of Registration, PICs and special/temporary permits. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 23.

q: Which section covers integration of the architecture profession?
n: Section 40 covers integration of the architecture profession into one national organization. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 40.

q: For an architectural firm formed with allied professionals, registered architects must hold at least what share?
n: An architectural firm or corporation formed with allied professionals must be at least 75% owned and controlled by registered architects. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 37.

q: You had a project for a client, a residential building. After the construction, you found out that the client used your design for another project without your consent. What will you do?
o: Ask to be paid for the design
File a case with the PRC
n: Reusing an architect's design for another project without written consent violates his ownership of the plans. He may demand compensation (the repeat-use fee) or take legal action. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 33; RA 8293 (Intellectual Property Code).

q: A Sth-year Architecture student is asked and contracted by his aunt to design a 2-storey residence for her. After the student finished preparing all the architectural plans, he asks his professor to sign and seal it. The professor agrees to do it for a sum of Php 6,000. Is there anything wrong with this practice? If yes, who is liable?
o: Yes, the architect is liable for this project
Yes, the student is liable for doing it
n: A student cannot practise architecture for a fee, and a professor who signs and seals plans he did not prepare or supervise is plan stamping. Both violate RA 9266. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 20(4), 23 and 29.

q: A 5th-year Architecture student is asked and contracted by his aunt to design a 2-storey residence for her. After the student finished preparing all the architectural plans, he asks his professor to sign and seal it. The professor agrees to do it for a sum of Php 6,000. What is the case if ever?
n: The professor-RLA who signs and seals the student's plans is liable to suspension or revocation, and the student to the penal clause for illegal practice. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 23 and 29.

q: Who provides Continuing Professional Education (CPE)?
n: Continuing professional education for architects is provided by the UAP, the accredited integrated professional organization, through CPD-accredited programs. Source: RA 10912 (CPD Act); RA 9266, Sec. 28 and 40.

q: What does RA 9266 allow that RA 545 did not?
n: RA 9266 allows corporate practice through registered architectural firms and corporations (Sec. 37), which the old RA 545 did not. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 37.

q: Under RA 9266, may an RLA do interior design for small projects?
n: Architectural interiors (space planning and interior design) are within the architect's scope of practice, so an RLA may design interiors for small projects. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3(4)(g).

q: What is the fine for a misdemeanor under RA 9266?
n: RA 9266's penal clause sets fines of ₱100,000 to ₱5,000,000. The court may also impose imprisonment of six months to six years, or both. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 29.

q: What is the prison term for a misdemeanor under RA 9266?
o: 6 months to 6 years, or fine and prison both
n: The penal clause provides imprisonment of six months to six years, or both fine and imprisonment, at the court's discretion. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 29.

q: Who is responsible for the implementation of RA 9266?
n: The Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture, under PRC supervision, implements and enforces RA 9266. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 7 and 44.

q: When may an architect prepare design concepts in parallel with other architects?
n: Preparing design concepts in parallel with other architects is proper only in design competitions held under accepted rules. Source: PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct; UAP Rules on Design Competitions.
